question: During internal jugular vein cannulation using the landmark technique, the needle is directed toward the ipsilateral nipple at a 45-degree angle to skin, with the head of the patient turned 30–45 degrees to the contralateral side.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is the correct landmark technique. Excessive head rotation (>45°) can collapse the IJ; the needle is directed toward the ipsilateral nipple. Revisit the anatomy block for the standard approach.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Head rotation of 30–45 degrees (not more, to avoid compressing the vein) and needle direction toward the ipsilateral nipple at ~45 degrees are the standard anatomical landmarks for the central/high approach to the internal jugular vein.
